G4533.definition: Salmon: Mat.1:4-5, Luk.3:32 (Σαλά, WH, R, mg.).†; (AS)

G4503.definition: Ῥoύθ, ἡ indecl. (Heb. רוּת), ; Ruth: Mat.15:1-39.†; (AS)

G4524.definition: Σαδώκ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. צָדוֹק, see supr., see word Σαδδουκαῖος) ; Sadoc, Zadok: Mat.1:14.†; (AS)

G4572.definition: (in NT not contracted, σαυτοῦ, as in Att..), ; reflex. prop. of 2nd of person(s) sing., used only in genitive, dative and accusative ; (of, to) thyself: Mat.4:6, Jhn.8:13, 1Ti.4:16, al. (In Hellenistic, the pl. is ἑαυτῶν (which see), not ὑμῶν αὐτῶν as in Attic, see Bl., § 13, 1.) †; (AS)

G4567.definition: (so also Sir 21:30, but in 3Ki.11:14, σατάν indecl.; Heb. שָׂטָן; Aram. סָטָנָא, whence the inflected Gk. form), ό, ; Satan (i.e. the adversary, as in LXX, ll. with): Mat.4:10 12:26, Mrk.1:13 3:23, 26 4:15 Luk.10:18 11:18 13:16 22:3, 31, Jhn.13:27, Act.5:3 26:18, Rom.16:20, 1Co.5:5 7:5, 2Co.2:11 11:14, 1Th.2:18, 2Th.2:9, 1Ti.1:20 5:15, Rev.2:9, 13 2:24 3:9 12:9 20:2, 7; addressed in person of Peter, Mat.16:23…

G4583.definition: σεληνιάζω; (σελήνη), ; act, in Manetho (Caren., 4, 81), in NT depon. -ομαι, ; to be moonstruck, i.e. epileptic (epilepsy being supposed to be influenced by the moon): Mat.4:24 17:15.†; (AS)

G4537.definition: to sound a trumpet: Rev.8:6 ff. Rev.9:1, 13 10:7 11:15; metaphorically, Mat.6:2. Impers., the trumpet sounds: 1Co.15:52.†; (AS)

G4505.definition: 1. in cl., the force, rush, swing, of a moving body; esp. of a charge of soldiers. ; 2. In late Greek (as in Macedonian, see Kennedy, Sources, 15), a narrow road, lane, street: in Polyb., of a road in camp; in LXX and NT (π. also) of streets in a town, Mat.6:2, Luk.14:21 Act.9:11 12:10 (cf. Rutherford, NPhr., 488).†; (AS)

G4594.definition: adv.,  ; to-day: Mat.6:11, Luk.4:21, Act.4:9, al.; opposite to αὔριον, Mat.6:30, Luk.12:28, Jas.4:13; χθὲς καὶ σ. καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας, Heb.13:8; ἡ σ. ἡμέρα, Act.20:20; ἕως (ἄχρι) τῆς σ. ἡμέρας, Rom.11:8, 2Co.3:14; μέχρι (ἕως) τῆς σ. (sc. ἡμέρας), Mat.11:23 27:8; as subst., τὸ σ., Heb.3:13; id. in appos., ὁρίζει ἡμὶραν, σ., Heb.4:7 R, mg., (see Westc., in l) ; (AS)

G4506.definition: to draw to oneself, hence, to rescue, deliver: with accusative of person(s), Mat.27:43, 2Pe.2:7; id. before ἀπό, Mat.6:13, Luk.11:4 (Rec., R, mg.), 2Ti.4:18; before ἐκ, Rom.7:24, 2Co.1:10, Col.1:13, 1Th.1:10, 2Ti.3:11, 2Pe.2:9; absol., ὁ ῥυύμενος, the deliverer, Rom.11:26. Passive: before ἀπό, Rom.15:31, 2Th.3:2; before ἐκ, Luk.1:74, 2Ti.4:17.†; (AS)

G4597.definition: a moth, clothes moth: Mat.6:19-20, Luk.12:33.†; (AS)

G4550.definition: rotten, corrupt, bad, worth­less: of trees and fruit (opposite to ἀγαθός, καλός), Mat.7:17-18 12:33 Luk.6:43; of fish, Mat.13:48. ; Metaphorical, in moral sense: λόγος σ., Eph.4:29. "In Hellenistic . . . it became a synonym for αἰσχρός or κακός," MM, xxii.†; (AS)

G4578.definition: (σείω),  ; a shaking, commotion, as a tempest at sea: Mat.8:24; esp. an earthquake: Mat.24:7 27:54 28:2, Mrk.13:8, Luk.21:11, Act.16:26, Rev.6:12 8:5 11:13, 19 16:18.†; (AS)

G4541.definition: (-ίτης, Τ; see WH, App., 154; BI., § 3, 4), -ον, ό, ; a Samaritan, i.e. an inhabitant of the city or the region of Samaria, in NT always the latter (see: Σαμαρία): Mat.10:5, Luk.9:52 10:33 17:16, Jhn.4:9, 39-40, Act.8:25; as an opprobrious epithet, Jhn.8:48.†; (AS)

G4531.definition: (σάλος),  ; prop., of the action of wind, storm, etc., to agitate, shake: of a reed, Mat.11:7, Luk.7:24; a house, Luk.6:48, Act.4:31 16:26; the earth, Heb.12:26; the heavenly bodies, Mat.24:29, Mrk.13:25, Luk.21:26; of a vessel shaken in filling, Luk.6:38. Metaphorical, ; (a) to shake, i.e. to render insecure: τὰ σαλευόμενα, τὰ μὴ., Heb.12:27; (b) with accusative of person(s), to cast down from a sense of security…

G4526.definition: (cf. Heb. שַׂק, which it renders in LXX), ; 1. a coarse cloth, sackcloth, usually made of hair: Rev.6:12. ; 2. Anything made of sackcloth; (a) a sack (Gen.42:25, al.); (b) a garment of sackcloth, expressive of mourning or penitence: Mat.11:21, Luk.10:13, Rev.11:3.†; (AS)

G4521.definition: σάββατον, -ου, τό (Aram. שַׁבָּתָא, transliterated σάββατα, and this being mistaken for a pl., the sing. σάββατον was formed from it), and σάββατα, -ων, τά; 1. the seventh day of the week, the sabbath ; (a) the sing. form -ον, τὸ σ.: Mat.12:8, Mrk.2:27, Luk.6:5, al.; ἡ ἡμέρα τοῦ σ. (in LXX, Exo.20:8, al., usually τῶν σ., see infr.), Luk.13:16 14:5; ὁδὸς σαββάτου, Act.1:12 (cf. Mat.24:29); dative, of time (τῷ) σ.…

G4570.definition: of fire or things on fire, to quench: with accusative, Mat.12:20, Eph.6:16, Heb.11:34; pass., Mat.25:8, Mrk.9:48, . Metaphorical (cf. Sng.8:7, 4Ma.16:4): τὸ πνεῦμα, 1Th.5:19.†; ζβέννυμι, for σβ-, 1Th.5:19 T (see WH, Notes, 148).†; (AS)

G4592.definition: a sign, mark, token; (a) of that which distinguishes a person or thing from others: Mat.26:48 Luk.2:12, 2Th.3:17 (cf. Deiss., LAE, 153.2); before genitive epexeg., Rom.4:11; with genitive obj., Mat.24:8, 30, 2Co.12:12; with genitive subj., Mat.16:3; (b) a sign of warning or admonition: Mat.12:39 16:4, Luk.2:34 11:29-30, 1Co.14:22; (with) a sign portending future events (Soph., Plat. al.): Mrk.13:4, Luk.21:7, 11…

G4563.definition: late form of σαίρω, ; to sweep: with accusative, Luk.15:8; pass., Mat.12:44, Luk.11:25.†; (AS)

G4568.definition: (Aram. סָאתָא = Heb. סְאָה),  ; a Hebrew measure (= about a peck and a half): Mat.13:33, Luk.13:21.†; (AS)

G4522.definition: a drag-net, seine: Mat.13:47.†; SYN.: ἀμφίβληστρον (which see), δίκτυον (AS)

G4576.definition: σέβω; to worship: with accusative of person(s), Mat.15:9, Mrk.7:7, Act.18:13 19:27; σεβόμενος τ. θεόν, Act.16:14 18:7; σεβόμενοι (σ. προσήλυτοι, σ. Ἕλληνες), devout, Act.13:43, 50 17:4, 17 (cf. προσήλυτος).†; (AS)

G4561.definition: flesh; 1. as in cl. generally, ; (a) prop., of the soft substance of the animal body: 1Co.15:39, 2Co.12:7, Gal.6:13, al.; σ. καὶ αἷμα, 1Co.5:50; σ. καὶ ὀστέα, Luk.24:39; pl., of the flesh of many or parts of the flesh of one (cl.), Rev.17:16 19:18; φαγεῖν, Re, ll. with (cf. κατεσθίειν, 4Ki.9:36, al., and βιβρώσκειν, frequently in l.); metaphorically, Jas.5:3; mystically, φ. (τρώγειν) τὴν σ. τοῦ υἱοῦ τ. ἀνθρώπου…

G4579.definition: to shake, move to and fro: τ. γῆν, Heb.12:26 (LXX); pass., ἡ γῆ, Mat.27:51 (LXX); συκῆ, Rev.6:13. Metaphorical, to agitate, stir up, with fear or some other emotion: Mat.21:10 28:4 (cf. ἀνα-, δια-, κατα-σείω).†; (AS)

G4536.definition: a trumpet, used in war and in religious ceremonies: 1Co.14:8, Heb.12:19, Rev.1:10 4:1 8:2, 6 8:11 9:14 By meton., a trumpet blast: μετὰ σ. μεγάλης, Mat.24:31; ἐν σ. θεοῦ, 1Th.4:16; ἐν τ. ἐσχάτῃ σ., 1Co.15:52.†; (AS)

G4518.definition: σαβαχθανεί (Rec. -νί; ζαφθανεί, Mt, l.with, WH, mg.) (Aram. שְׁבַקְתַּנִי), ; sabachthani, i.e. thou host forsaken me: Mat.27:46, Mrk.15:34 (Psa.22:2, Heb. עָזַב).†; ζαφθανεί (cf. Heb. עָזַב), ; zaphthanei: Mat.27:46 (WH, mg., for Rec. σεβαχθανεί, which see; "probably an attempt to reproduce the Heb. as disting from Aram. forms," WE, Notes, 21; cf. also Dalman, Words, 53 f.).†; (AS)

G4511.definition: (ῥέω),  ; a flowing, issue: τ. αἵματος, Mrk.5:25, Luk.8:43-44.†; (AS)

G4547.definition: (dimin. of σάνδαλον, prob. Persian),  ; a sandal: Mrk.6:9, Act.12:8.†; (AS)

G4501.definition: a large broad sword, used by the Thracians (see DB, iv, 634); then generally (in LXX used interchangeably with μάχαιρα, which see), a sword: Rev.1:16 2:12, 16 6:8 19:15, 21; metaphorically, Luk.2:35.†; (AS)

G4527.definition: Sala, Shalah: Luk.3:32 (R, txt., Σαλμών, which see), Luk.3:35.†; (AS)

G4562.definition: Σερούχ (Rec. Σαρ-), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. שְׂרוּג), ; Serug: Luk.3:35.† ; (AS)

G4558.definition: Sarepta, a city of Sidon: Luk.4:26.†; (AS)

G4540.definition: Σαμαρία (Rec. -άρεια), -ας, ἡ (Heb. שֹׁמְרוֹן; Aram. שָׁמְרַיִן), ; Samaria; (a) the city: Act.8:5 (and perhaps also Act.8:9, 14); (b) the region: Luk.17:11, Jhn.4:4-5, 7, Act.1:8 8:1 (and perhaps also Act.8:9, 14) Act.9:31 15:3.†; (AS)

G4535.definition: in poets and late prose, a tossing, as of an earthquake; esp. the tossing, the rolling swell of the sea: Luk.21:25.†; (AS)

G4530.definition: Salim: Jhn.3:23 (see Westc., in l; DB, iii, 354).†; (AS)

G4542.definition: 1. in FlJ (B.J., i, 21, 2, al.), the region of Samaria. ; 2. a Samaritan woman: Jhn.4:9.†; (AS)

G4591.definition: (σῆμα, a sign),  ; to give a sign, signify, indicate: with accusative of thing(s), Act.25:27, Rev.1:1 (cf. MM, xxii); with accusative and inf., Act.11:28; before quæst. indir., Jhn.12:33 18:32 21:19.†; (AS)

G4545.definition: (in FlJ, Σαμούηλος; Heb. שְׁמוּאֵל), ; Samuel (1Ki.1:20, al.): Act.3:24 13:20, Heb.11:32.†; (AS)

G4551.definition: Σαπφείρα, -ης (see B1., § 3, 4), ἡ ; (Aram. שַׁפִּירָא) ; Sapphia: Act.5:1.†; (AS)

G4549.definition: (in FlJ, Σάουλος; Heb. שָׁאוּל) ; Saul; (a) the King of Israel: Act.13:21; (b) the Jewish name of the Apostle Paul, used in the indecl. form only in address (cf. Σαῦλος): Act.9:4, 17 22:7, 13 26:14.†; (AS)

G4581.definition: Σελευκία (Rec. -εύκεια), ; Seleucia, a city of Syria: Act.13:4.† ; (AS)

G4529.definition: Salamis, the chief city of Cyprus: Act.13:5.†; (AS)

G4517.definition: to strengthen; most frequently in pf., ἔρρωμαι, to put forth strength, be strong, hence, often in imperat., ἔρρωσο, ἔρρωσθε, farewell (Lat. vale): Act.15:29 23:30 Rec., R, mg.†; (AS)

G4543.definition: (-θράκη, BE), -ης, ἡ ; Samothrace, an island in the Ægean: Act.16:11.†; (AS)

G4544.definition: Samos, an island in the Ægean: Act.20:15.†; (AS)

G4575.definition: 1. reverend, august. ; 2. In late writers, with reference to the Roman Imperial name; (a) ὁ Σ., Augustus, i.e. the Roman Emperor: Act.25:21, 25; (b) Augustan: σπείρα σ., Act.27:1 (See further, Deiss., BS, 218.) †; (AS)

G4534.definition: Salmone, a promontory of Crete: Act.27:7.†; (AS)

G4573.definition: (σέβας, reverential awe),  ; 1. to fear (Hom). ; 2. In later writers, = σέβομαι, to worship: Rom.1:25 ; (AS)

G4560.definition: (σάρξ),  ; = Lat. carneus (the termination -ινος denoting the substance or material of a thing; see Tr., Syn., § LXXii; Lft., Notes, 184; and for illustrations from π., see MM, xxii), of the flesh, of flesh, fleshy (Plat., Arist., Plut., al.): Rom.7:14, 1Co.3:1, 2Co.3:3, Heb.7:16. (Rec. has -ικός in all these passages except 2Co.3:3, but the evidence is decisive against it.)†; SYN.: σαρκικός, q.v (AS)

G4519.definition: Sabaoth, i.e. hosts or armies (see DB, l.with): Rom.9:29 (LXX), Ja 54.†; (AS)

G4559.definition: (seel. for σάρκινος, Arist., H.A., x, 2, 7) ; = Lat. carnalis, i.e. ; (a) associated with or pertaining to the flesh, fleshly, carnal: Rom.15:27, 1Co.9:11; (b) in a more ethical sense, of the nature of the flesh, under the control of its appetites, fleshly, carnal, sensual (but including more than mere sensuality; cf. Hort, 1Pe., 133): 1Co.3:3, 2Co.1:12 10:4, 1Pe.2:11.†; SYN.: σάρκινος (which see), ψυχικός; cf. Tr.…

G4553.definition: 1. a plaited rope (Æsch.). ; 2. a hamper, a basket made of ropes: 2Co.11:33.†; (AS)

G4512.definition: a fold or pucker in the face, a wrinkle , Lat. ruga, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G4586.definition: (σέβομαι),  ; 1. reverend, august, venerable, in cl. of the gods and also of human beings. ; 2. grave, serious; of persons: 1Ti.3:8 3:11, Tit.2:2; of things: Php.4:8 (see Tr., Syn., § xcii; Cremer, 37; MM, xxii).†; (AS)

G4525.definition: 1. prop. (Hom., al.), of dogs, to wag the tail, fawn. ; 2. Metaphorical, of persons, with accusative, to fawn upon, flatter, beguile: pass., 1Th.3:3 (for conjectural emendations of the text, see ICC, and M, Th., in l).†; (AS)

G4593.definition: (σημεῖον),  ; to mark, note. Mid., to note for oneself: 2Th.3:14 (frequently in π.; see ICC, M, Th., in l).†; (AS)

G4587.definition: (σεμνός),  ; gravity: 1Ti.2:2 3:4 (Vg. eastitas, cf. Soph., Lex., and Zorell, see word), Tit.2:7.† ; (AS)

G4520.definition: (σαββατίζω, to keep the sabbath, Exo.16:30, al.), ; a keeping sabbath, a sabbath rest: metaphorically, as in Mishna (Zorell, see word), Heb.4:9.†; (AS)

G4507.definition: (ῥυπαρός) ; filthiness: metaphorically, of moral defile­ment, Jas.1:21.†; (AS)

G4508.definition: (ῥύπος),  ; filthy, dirty: of old, shabby clothing (Za, l.with), Jas.2:2; metaphorically, of moral defilement, Rev.22:11.†; (AS)

G4595.definition: to make corrupt: 2 pf. act, with mid, sense (see M, Pr., 154), σέσηπεν, has perished, become corrupted, Jas.5:2.†; (AS)

G4577.definition: 1. (a) a cord; (b) a chain (cf. Pr., l.with): σειραὶ ζόφου, 2Pe.2:4, Rec., R, mg. (see: σειρός). ; 2. a lock of hair (Jg, ll. with).†; (AS)

G4500.definition: adv. (ῥοῖζος, the whistling of an arrow), ; with rushing sound (as of roaring flames): 2Pe.3:10.†; (AS)

G4554.definition: Sardis, the chief city of Lydia: Rev.1:11 3:1, 4 ; (AS)

G4556.definition: the sardian stone, sard (of which carnelian is one variety): Rev.4:3 21:20.†; (AS)

G4596.definition: σιρικός (by assimilation of vowels, for σηρικός; see Mayser, 150; WH, Notes, 151), -ή, -όν ; (οἱ Σῆρες, a people of India from whom the ancients got the first silk), ; silk, silken; as subst., τὸ σ., silken fabric, silk: Rev.18:12 (cf. FlJ, B.J., vii, 5, 4).†; (AS)

G4538.definition: (so Inscr. and late writers for Mt. σαλπιγκτής), οῦ, ὁ, ; a trumpeter: Rev.18:22.†; (AS)

G4557.definition: (σάρδιον, ὄνυξ), ; sardonyx, a stone marked by the red of the sard and the white of the onyx: Rev.21:20.†; (AS)

G4510.definition: (ῥύπος), ; to make filthy: Rev.22:11 Rec. (AV, tr. as = ῥυπάω, to be filthy).†; (AS)
